chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from Al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Manqari, who said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to me, and I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Regarding the words of the Exalted God: 'He let loose the two seas, meeting together: Between them is a Barrier which they do not transgress.' He said: Ali and Fatimah (peace be upon them) are two seas of knowledge, deep, neither one transgresses against the other. 'Out of them come pearls and coral' refers to Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (peace be upon them).

key_terms.مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ: He let loose the two seas

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia interpretation of the 'two seas' and 'barrier' in Surah Ar-Rahman?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Al-Sadiq (AS) provides a metaphysical interpretation of Surah Ar-Rahman, identifying Ali and Fatimah (AS) as the 'two seas' of divine knowledge that remain distinct yet complementary, while Hasan and Husayn (AS) are the precious 'pearls and coral' derived from them. This exegesis highlights the unique epistemological status of the Ahl al-Bayt, portraying them as the primary sources from which the virtues and spiritual treasures of the Imams emerge without confusion or transgression.
